name: Mandirapureeswarar Temple, Tiruvusathanam (Kovilur)
deity: Shiva as Mandirapureeswarar (the lord who gave counsel), with the goddess Periyanayaki (Brihannayaki)
period: Tevaram era (hymned 7th century); later Chola structural temple
summary: Kovilur, the Tevaram's Tiruvusathanam, near Muthupettai in the southern delta, honours Shiva as Mandirapureeswarar — the lord of counsel — with the goddess Periyanayaki. A Paadal Petra Sthalam hymned by Tirugnana Sambandar, its name recalls the tradition that Rama sought Shiva's counsel here before building the bridge to Lanka.

sections.history: Kovilur, whose Tevaram name is Tiruvusathanam (Tiru Usaatthanam), lies in the southern delta, about 3 km north of Muthupettai on the Muthupettai–Mannargudi road, some 22 km from Pattukottai (sources place it in Tiruvarur or Thanjavur district). It is a Paadal Petra Sthalam, hymned in the Tevaram by Tirugnana Sambandar. The stone temple is of the Chola period and later.
sections.architecture: A Dravidian temple of the lower delta, the shrine enshrines Mandirapureeswarar in the sanctum, with the goddess Periyanayaki — also Brihannayaki, 'the great mother' — in her own shrine, a Nandi and the parivara devatas. The temple keeps the simple, well-ordered plan of the smaller delta sanctuaries.
sections.legends: The names of place and lord both turn on counsel. Tiru Usaatthanam means 'the holy place of consultation,' and Mandirapureeswarar is 'the lord of mandira, of counsel.' By tradition Rama came here before his campaign against Ravana and sought Shiva's counsel on building the great bridge, the Setu, to Lanka; the lord gave his blessing and advice, and so the place keeps the memory of that divine consultation. To worship here is held to bring wise counsel and right decision to the devotee.
sections.festivals: The temple observes Maha Shivaratri in Masi (February–March), Navaratri in Purattasi (September–October) and the Mondays of Karthikai, with Pradosha worship, at the quiet scale of a village shrine. Pilgrims on the Paadal Petra trail of the southern delta include Kovilur among their stops.
sections.experience: At Kovilur the pilgrim comes to a shrine of divine counsel, where Rama is said to have sought Shiva's advice before the bridge to Lanka. Before Mandirapureeswarar, lord of counsel, and the great mother Periyanayaki, the visitor brings the questions of the heart to a quiet Tevaram temple of the southern Kaveri country.

visit.timings: Typically open from early morning to midday and again from late afternoon into the evening; confirm timings locally, especially on festival days.
visit.dressCode: Modest traditional attire is expected, with shoulders and knees covered; footwear is left at the entrance.
visit.photography: Photography is generally allowed in the outer corridors but not inside the sanctum; ask temple staff before photographing rituals.
visit.gettingThere: Kovilur is about 3 km north of Muthupettai on the Muthupettai–Mannargudi road, roughly 22 km from Pattukottai, in the southern Kaveri delta. Muthupettai and Pattukottai are the nearest towns, with buses and taxis to the village; Thanjavur and Thiruthuraipoondi are the nearest rail heads.
